## Summary

Bring Nemotron 3.5 Super MTP serving optimizations for SM120 into SGLang: small-M NVFP4 MoE execution, SM120 GEMV, FlashInfer host planning, and hybrid prefill CUDA graphs.

## Scope

- Native SM120 NVFP4 MoE for 1–4 token rows on Nemotron's expert shape, dispatched from the FlashInfer CUTLASS runner when FlashInfer's fused finalize is enabled. Unsupported shapes and quantization recipes keep the stock runner.
- Opt-in reversible pair-major FC2 weight layout for serial verify (`SGLANG_SM120_NVFP4_PHASE_LAYOUT`). Nemotron owns the layout, and the runner reaches it through an optional `prepare_for_forward` hook. Weight updates reuse the existing derived-cache guard, and weight export is rejected while the layout is enabled.
- The BF16 and FP8 GEMV kernels gain PDL and SM120-tuned launch shapes. `--bf16-gemm-backend gemv` is accepted on SM12x.
- An opt-in M=2–16 Triton router inside the existing fused-gate operator (`SGLANG_SM120_MTP_ROUTER_TOP22`), with unchanged device arithmetic.
- Opt-in FlashInfer host planning for EAGLE draft and verify (`SGLANG_FLASHINFER_DRAFT_HOST_INDPTR`, `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_VERIFY_HOST_PLAN`).
- Hybrid prefill CUDA graphs for Nemotron on SM120, with shared experts overlapped on one explicit stream.
- The logits processor, Eagle worker, top-k dispatcher and Mamba SSD kernels are unchanged from main.
- Upstream changes this PR previously carried are no longer part of it:
  - #34535 (DP request-split floor and DP decode-relabel fixes, with their tests) stays under its own review.
  - The #42746 prefill-then-decode regression test is dropped. Main already keeps fmha_v2 out of XQA's workspace semaphores through #42930, which superseded #42746.
  - #43685 (Nemotron-H EPLB) and #43054 (DFLASH verify mask policy) are in main. This PR relies on main's MoE `forward_batch` plumbing instead of duplicating it.
- The diff now contains **23 files, +1,825/−58 lines**, down from 38 files, +2,111/−80.

## Validation

For this revision (`4631e828b8`), only CPU and static checks were run, on macOS:
- `git diff --check`, the repository's pinned ruff 0.15.1 (hook rule selection and format check), isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, clang-format 20.1.7, `check-ast`, `debug-statements`, and the registered-test lint scripts all pass on the changed files.
- A focused CPU check confirms the Nemotron-H MoE decoder layers, including the MTP layer, still pass `forward_batch` to the MoE core (the input the SM120 prefill-overlap gate reads). Results match the previous head `d3f59dd9a6`.
- Eight CPU-registered Nemotron-H unit test files give identical results on this revision, the previous head and main. In each case 151 pass and 1 is skipped. The remaining 134 fail on all three in this Mac environment; sampled failures hit the Torch ≥ 2.13 MPS requirement (the available environment has Torch 2.11).

No GPU tests, E2E serving runs or benchmarks were run for this revision.

### Historical E2E evidence (not rerun)

The measurements below come from earlier heads, before main was merged (`d3f59dd9a6`) and before the carried upstream changes were removed. Both measured heads still included the carried changes. They compare the earlier public head `af2628444e` with the cleanup head `ce427d4d9b`. Both ran on the same RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), EA1008 NVFP4 checkpoint, pinned container, launch settings and request token IDs. Settings: TP=1, concurrency=1, real EAGLE acceptance (3 steps / 4 draft tokens). Each run has two warmups and 80 measured requests of 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens, with the prefix cache flushed before every measured request.

| Check | `af2628444e` | `ce427d4d9b` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput | 243.6717 tokens/s | 242.6594 tokens/s |
| Mean TTFT | 845.7203 ms | 858.7892 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 3.2812 ms | 3.2856 ms |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.9798 | 3.9798 |
| Same fixed 100-question GSM8K slice | 95/100 | 95/100 |

Throughput changed by **-0.42%** and TTFT by **+13.07 ms (+1.55%)**. All 80 complete output-token sequences and all 100 GSM8K answer texts match exactly. Both runs had zero cached prompt tokens, zero request retractions, and no competing GPU process during measurement. The workload uses repeated text and has high acceptance. These results do not establish general conversational throughput or performance on other GPU architectures.

Earlier hardware recipes and model-support validation are recorded in [cookbook PR #44510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44510).

+        a2.view(-1),
